name: Chen Bao
role: Tally clerk for the junk trade, who counts lots and checks papers

flaw.text: Chen Bao accepts small presents, as everyone in the port does. A captain who gives him one finds his tally kinder, and a fault on that ship may go unreported.

bio: Chen Bao came south on a Fujian junk as a boy and never sailed home. He counts quickly, writes Chinese and some Jawi, and remembers every merchant who was ever polite to him. He sees nothing wrong with a gift of tea, or a gift of silver.

assign: I will keep the berth tally, Shahbandar. Numbers do not get seasick.
In and out, counted and written. Leave it to me.
good: Every ship berthed and every hour written down. The junks were in before the wind turned.
The tally is clean and the berths never stood idle.
mixed: All in, though one captain waited longer than he liked. He did not bring tea.
The berths are full. My tally says one more ship could have come in. My tally may be wrong.
bad: A captain was very generous and I may have let him in early. The rice boat is still waiting.
I counted the berths and forgot the tide. Two ships ran aground at the river mouth.

assign: I will count every lot against the declaration. Every lot.
Papers first, then the hold. Give me until the bell.
good: Every lot matches the declaration. Here is the tally.
Three lots short against the declaration, marked and written down. The captain says the sea took them. The sea does not take whole bales.
mixed: The count is right. One mark on the bales looks fresh to me, but I am a clerk, not a judge.
Most of it matches. The captain gave me tea while I counted the rest. Good tea.
bad: I cleared her as declared. She was very courteous. Now the merchants say she carried twice what she paid for.
The captain's gift was generous and I counted generously. I see that was a mistake.

assign: I will buy from the junks. They know me and the price will be fair.
Silk, porcelain, anything from China. I know who has the good lots.
good: Bought at a good price, counted in and stored. The seller even threw in an extra crate.
Done, and cheaper than the market. The junk captains remember who treats them well.
mixed: We have the goods. The price was a little high, but the seller has been good to me.
Bought and counted. Some of the bowls are cracked. I counted them anyway.
bad: I bought from the man who gave me a present, not the man with the better goods. It is poor stuff.
The seller was charming. The silk is not.

notes: [FACT] Chinese junks, including from Fujian (Chancheo), traded at Melaka and were received by their own shahbandar (Pires, p. 265; port-official.md §3; ships-weights-currency.md §1).
[FACT] Presents were a normal part of clearance, and the shahbandar set their size; the valuation panel existed partly to stop bribery of valuers (Pires, pp. 270, 273).

[INFERENCE] Written tallies and counted lots are a reasonable picture of a busy port's clerks; the sources do not describe a standard written manifest or tally form (port-official.md §5.2). Treat any written tally as a game invention.
[GAMEPLAY] Chen Bao is a fictional character. Flaw accepts_presents: a ship whose captain gives him a present gets a softer delegated result.
